tasks.short: Receive service requests, clarify requirements and prepare work orders for dispatch.

steps.what: Read emailed service requests and identify the requested work.

loop.output: Request fields with source passages and explicit missing values.
loop.check: Validate required fields, formats and source support; flag conflicting instructions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per request; send unresolved fields to the dispatcher.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests describe locations, faults and access instructions in varied free text.

steps.what: Check customer, site and equipment details against existing records.
Call the requester to resolve missing details, urgency and access arrangements.
Determine service scope, priority and required skills or equipment.
Enter the work order using the agreed service requirements.
Check the completed order and release it to the dispatch queue.

tasks.design: A reusable intake template in {WORKFLOW} receives requests from {EMAIL}; a bounded extraction loop proposes fields and deterministic checks match records in {CRM} and {OPS_SYSTEM}. Configured forms generate the draft work order, while the dispatcher resolves ambiguity and approves release to the dispatch queue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Request formats vary, reference records disagree and connecting the mailbox to operational records took bespoke work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and interfaces handle structured requests; bounded extraction handles variable text, and AI-assisted coding reduces adapter development effort.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous urgency, incomplete site information and unreliable reference records still require operational judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when a routine request conceals a dangerous fault, unrealistic promise or sensitive customer situation.

ambition.what: A request-readiness check that identifies missing access details before scheduling.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends less time copying requests and more time resolving unclear work before it reaches crews. They can return incomplete requests for clarification; spending and service-promise authority do not automatically expand.

reach.task: Check whether incoming work is sufficiently defined for scheduling.
reach.learn: Scope boundaries, acceptance criteria and dependency checks.

evidence.claim: PDF order extraction is an existing capability; applying it to service requests needs local validation.
Integrated operational systems already maintain transport and warehouse records.
Deterministic matching, required-field checks and work-order templates can handle structured intake.

assumptions: The baseline is a mobile service operation within a company of 200 to 2,000 staff.
Some requests arrive through email, while operational records already reside in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
The reusable intake schema can be prepared independently; live processing requires authorised company access.
GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act applicability depends on the implemented use.
unknowns: Actual request channels, volumes and attachment formats.
Available interfaces and customer or equipment identifiers.
Local priority rules and who may release work orders.
Applicable national rules and employee consultation arrangements.
research_questions: Which existing {OPS_SYSTEM} intake features cover the required fields?
Which request ambiguities cause the most dispatch rework?
Can extraction preserve every safety-relevant instruction in a representative sample?
new_work: Review extracted fields and resolve unmatched records.
Maintain intake schemas, validation rules and connector mappings.
Sample released orders for omitted instructions and incorrect priorities.
Maintain access controls and request-data retention.

tasks.short: Maintain dispatch records for requests, completed work, charges, expenses and inventory movements.

steps.what: Record crew updates, work completion and service details against the work order.
Transfer charge, expense and parts details into the relevant financial records.
Compare entries with supporting records and investigate missing or conflicting details.
Approve operational corrections and release charge details for finance processing.
File supporting documents and link them to the dispatch record.
Copy dispatch totals into the shared shift summary.

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} to capture structured service events once, link evidence in {DOCS} and transfer validated charge and inventory details to {ERP}. Deterministic reconciliation sends discrepancies to an approval queue, while a saved operational view replaces the duplicate shift workbook in {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work-order identifiers, financial codes and supporting documents were disconnected, making manual copying the practical bridge.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured event capture and deterministic adapters can reuse existing records; AI-assisted coding makes company-specific mappings cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Late crew updates, disputed charges, accounting cut-offs and incorrect parts usage still need investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a missing update from a disputed service outcome and deciding which evidence supports a correction.

ambition.what: Review unresolved charge exceptions each shift instead of waiting for billing preparation.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher becomes an exception investigator rather than a duplicate record keeper. They gain visibility of unresolved charge evidence; finance retains accounting and invoice approval rights.

reach.task: Reconcile parts issued, used and returned against a service job.
reach.learn: Inventory transaction types, units of measure and correction controls.

evidence.claim: Operational transport systems already combine multiple categories of logistics records.
Integrated creation and signing of transport documents demonstrates linked operational evidence.
A vendor customer case reports reduced invoicing administration; it does not establish dispatcher-specific savings.
Identifier-based reconciliation and duplicate prevention need deterministic rules rather than a model.

assumptions: Crews can supply structured completion, parts and expense events; missing events remain exceptions.
Supporting documents can be linked using a work-order identifier without interpreting their free text.
The shift workbook duplicates information available from operational records.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates; no crew work is assumed to disappear.
GDPR requires appropriate access and retention; employee logging may require consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Which records are authoritative for charges, inventory and completion.
Whether crew event capture is already available and used reliably.
Financial posting permissions, approval limits and retention requirements.
Whether the shift summary contains unique information that must be retained.
Applicable employee consultation and access requirements.
research_questions: Can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} configuration replace the duplicate workbook?
Which reconciliation checks detect financially material errors?
How will retries avoid duplicate inventory movements and charge records?
new_work: Investigate missing events, duplicates and mismatched financial codes.
Maintain rate mappings and reconciliation tolerances.
Monitor failed transfers and reconcile transfer totals.
Review document access, retention and correction logs.

tasks.short: Coordinate repairs and recovery plans when vehicles or equipment interrupt scheduled service.

steps.what: Receive the breakdown call and establish immediate service and safety implications.
Check equipment history, warranty, assigned jobs and available replacement resources.
Call maintenance providers to establish repair availability, likely delays and alternatives.
Choose repair or replacement by comparing downtime, service commitments and cost.
Approve exceptional spending or service trade-offs beyond the dispatcher's delegated limits.
Book the selected repair and communicate equipment location and access details.
Revise affected jobs and resource assignments around the expected repair window.
Confirm technical clearance before returning repaired equipment to service.

tasks.design: Configured views in {OPS_SYSTEM} assemble the incident, equipment history and affected jobs; deterministic comparisons show recovery options and feasible schedule revisions. A flow in {WORKFLOW} prepares repair instructions for approval and sends them through {EMAIL}, while provider negotiation, exceptional spending and technical clearance remain human decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repair coordination combines incomplete fault information, uncertain provider availability and service trade-offs across separate records.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can feed a reusable recovery brief, while inexpensive deterministic code compares scenarios and prepares the paperwork.
tasks.still_hard: Diagnosis, uncertain repair times, supplier commitments and competing customer consequences remain situational.
tasks.human_edge: Securing a credible repair commitment and choosing which disruption the operation can tolerate.

ambition.what: An incident recovery brief comparing repair and replacement before a booking decision.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher spends more time negotiating recovery and less time assembling histories or rewriting schedules. They gain clearer choices within existing delegated limits; exceptional spending and technical clearance keep their current approvers.

reach.task: Define fallback resources for the loss of a critical vehicle or equipment type.
reach.learn: Recovery priorities, dependency mapping and minimum service levels.

evidence.claim: Deterministic constraint checks can compare recovery schedules, but repair uncertainty still requires human judgement.
Operational systems offer an existing base for transport and resource records; this does not prove repair coordination automation.
A vendor case documents benefits from appointment scheduling in freight operations, an adjacent rather than equivalent use.

assumptions: The scope is coordination and administration; physical diagnosis and repair are excluded.
Provider negotiation remains a conversation, so no model loop is required.
Exceptional approval is conditional; its share represents average effort across repair incidents.
Routine plans within delegated limits bypass exceptional spending approval.
Schedule revisions enter the normal dispatch release process before crews act.
Time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates.
GDPR and applicable national rules govern personal data and changed working arrangements.
unknowns: Actual spending limits and escalation responsibilities.
Availability and quality of equipment history and replacement-resource records.
Provider booking channels, cancellation terms and access requirements.
Who is authorised to certify equipment for return to service.
Applicable employee consultation requirements for schedule changes.
research_questions: Which recovery choices can be compared using reliable cost and downtime inputs?
Can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} views assemble the recovery brief?
How should the system handle uncertain repair estimates without creating false commitments?
new_work: Maintain provider contacts, spending limits and fallback-resource rules.
Resolve failed bookings and changes to repair estimates.
Check that schedule revisions reach the normal release queue.
Record technical clearance and review unresolved incidents.

tasks.short: Track crew and equipment availability, identify service risks and coordinate schedule changes.

steps.what: Inspect location and job-status screens for crew availability, delays and idle equipment.
Contact crews when location or availability is missing, stale or inconsistent.
Calculate busy time, waiting time and available capacity in the shift workbook.
Compare open jobs with available crews, equipment, qualifications and remaining working time.
Choose reassignments after considering service urgency, crew context and customer commitments.
Transmit changed assignments and practical instructions to the affected crews.
Acknowledge the assignment or report a practical obstacle.

tasks.design: Configure {OPS_SYSTEM} to show fresh resource status and acknowledge assignments; deterministic jobs on {DATA_PLATFORM} calculate utilisation and feasible schedule candidates using authorised roster data from {HCM}. The dispatcher approves reassignments and instruction release, while stale data, infeasible jobs and missing acknowledgements enter an exception queue in {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Location feeds, crew updates and rosters were disconnected, while scheduling rules were held in dispatchers' experience.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing event feeds, configurable alerts and deterministic solvers can be joined more cheaply with AI-assisted coding; no autonomous agent is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Stale signals, uncertain job duration and unrecorded crew constraints can make a mathematically feasible schedule impractical.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding why a crew appears idle and balancing customer urgency with safe, workable assignments.

ambition.what: Reassess threatened service windows whenever a material delay or equipment outage occurs.

tasks.altitude: The dispatcher moves from repeatedly scanning screens to reviewing a ranked exception queue and feasible alternatives. They can propose earlier recovery within existing dispatch authority; employment and disciplinary decisions remain outside this tool.

reach.task: Identify recurring capacity bottlenecks by time window and resource type.
reach.learn: Event-data quality, queue measures and the difference between utilisation and service performance.

evidence.claim: Operational transport systems provide an existing foundation for dispatch records and resource coordination.
A documented vendor case reports reduced truck turnaround through appointment scheduling; it does not validate workforce tracking.
AI used for certain worker allocation, monitoring or evaluation purposes can fall within Annex III employment provisions.
In the Netherlands, working-time arrangements and certain employee monitoring systems involve works-council consent provisions.
Freshness checks, utilisation calculations and constraint-based schedule candidates can use deterministic technology.

assumptions: Operational location or check-in data already exists; new tracking hardware is outside these build estimates.
The baseline includes a supplementary capacity workbook, not spreadsheet-based dispatch throughout.
The scheduler uses explicit operational constraints rather than inferred personality or behavioural scores.
Qualification and availability data is limited to what dispatch genuinely needs.
GDPR applies to identifiable location and activity data; employee agreement alone is not assumed to establish a lawful basis.
National consultation and employment rules vary; EU AI Act classification depends on the final system and purpose.
Time shares and remaining effort are estimates; the final acknowledgement step includes adjacent worker effort.
Consultation and access ranges are provisional and can extend the rollout calendar.
unknowns: Location-data coverage, freshness, lawful basis and retention policy.
Whether off-duty tracking can be disabled.
Actual working-time, break, qualification and assignment constraints.
Available mobile acknowledgement features and roster interfaces.
Applicable national consultation requirements and existing employee agreements.
Current delegated reassignment authority.
research_questions: Which operational exceptions can existing {OPS_SYSTEM} alerts already detect?
How often do stale events create false capacity signals?
Does the proposed scheduling component qualify as an AI system, and which obligations apply?
Which utilisation measures help dispatch without encouraging unsafe speed or unfair comparisons?
new_work: Resolve stale signals, missed acknowledgements and infeasible schedule candidates.
Maintain qualifications, working-time constraints and alert thresholds.
Monitor connector reliability and suppress duplicate alerts.
Review location-data access, retention and employee consultation commitments.
Check whether suggested assignments systematically disadvantage particular groups or shifts.

role.altitude: The dispatcher spends less of the week entering records, scanning screens and assembling recovery paperwork. More time goes to clarifying requests, negotiating repairs and approving workable schedule changes; decision rights expand only through explicit delegation.
reach: Project management specialist: improve request readiness and scope definition.
Shipping, receiving and inventory clerk: reconcile job-level parts movements.
Business continuity planner: define practical fallback resources.
Logistics analyst: investigate recurring capacity bottlenecks.
skills_to_grow: Define reusable operational records and identifiers.
Translate dispatch constraints into testable rules.
Read exception queues and assess data freshness.
Understand employee-data access and consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a service-recovery desk that spots threatened commitments early, prepares feasible alternatives and coordinates approved action across crews, maintenance and customer-facing teams.

job.title: Dispatchers, Except Police, Fire, and Ambulance
